reason: The text demonstrates that non-leaders exercise significant agency. Eve (the woman) independently assesses the forbidden tree ('the woman saw that the tree was good for food'), makes her own decision to eat from it ('and she took of its fruit, and ate'), and takes action to give it to Adam. Adam similarly chooses to eat the fruit when offered. Neither Eve nor Adam are presented as leaders, yet both make autonomous decisions and take consequential actions. Only God could be described as a leader in this passage, yet the text clearly shows that agency—the capacity to make choices and act—is not exclusive to leaders.
